gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Loud, poured-ink letters with a high mean line, all cut from one stubborn width, lead the way in Luckiest Guy. Noto Sans Avestan is the foil: a plain sans with a tall x-height and curves that stop short.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-balinese: Noto Sans Balinese reads with a breathing space inside every curve and short ascenders that stay low. And Luckiest Guy does the opposite job, shouting in cheerful, uniform strokes that never thicken on the downstrokes.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Cheerful is the first word for Luckiest Guy, whose glyphs look cut from strips of equal width and earn their keep big and short. Noto Sans Bamum brings big open counters and curves that end before they turn inward.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-bassa-vah: Luckiest Guy sets a loud, cheerful tone with a high mean line and strokes as steady as a drawn string. Noto Sans Bassa Vah, a plain sans with a dominant midsection and pliers-like c, makes the strongest contrast.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-batak: Cheerful ink that looks traced with a marker, set under a high mean line, gives Luckiest Guy its loud personality. Noto Sans Batak counters with a towering x-height, a plain sans that never squeezes its e shut.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Contemporary in feel, Noto Sans Bengali keeps its capitals barely above the lowercase and its letter mouths distinctly open. And a longer passage in it would move along easily, while Luckiest Guy keeps its bars as heavy as its stems.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-bhaiksuki: Strokes like a bent paperclip, loud and cheerful under a high mean line, are what stand out in Luckiest Guy. Noto Sans Bhaiksuki, a plain sans with swollen lowercase, keeps the page readable.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Luckiest Guy draws plain constant-width lines under a high mean line, loud and cheerful from the first letter. Noto Sans Brahmi follows with open-ended curves, so a longer passage would feel light and unhurried.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-buginese: Chunky, cheerful, and loud: Luckiest Guy has no hairlines and no swells anywhere. But Noto Sans Buginese is the quiet one, with open letter mouths like unjoined chalk arcs and short ascenders.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-buhid: Noto Sans Buhid sets generous space between its curve ends and stems, with a high-set x-height. And Luckiest Guy sits against it like a ballpoint-drawn shout, cheerful and loud, so the two feel like a joke and its straight man.
